front.title: Key-Value (KV) Cache Block Transfer Protocol (KBTP) over RDMA: Block Load, Mapped Store, and Unmapped Store

abstract.t: Inference systems move key-value (KV) cache blocks between instances and cache tiers over RDMA. Existing practice forces a choice between statically registered remote memory, which is fast but wastes memory, and per-transfer remote procedure calls, which use memory well but involve the target's CPU in every transfer. This document specifies the KV Cache Block Transfer Protocol (KBTP), an upper-layer protocol over RDMA with three operations: Block Load, which places a stored block into the initiator's memory; Block Mapped Store, which writes a block into an already allocated block; and Block Unmapped Store, which allocates a free block at the target and writes it in one operation. KBTP defines the request and completion messages, a block table, and a free-block ring whose counters use masked atomic fetch- and-add. These structures are designed so that a target can execute loads and stores within its RDMA network interface, and allocations as well where the interface supports conditional execution, without involving its CPU per operation, while remaining interoperable with targets that process requests in software. KBTP is bound to RDMAP with the RDMA protocol extensions, and can also be used over InfiniBand and RoCEv2.
